Tucker Center]] |champion = |tourney = [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |tourney_result = Sweet Sixteen }} {{2020–21 ACC men's basketball standings}} The '''2020–21 Florida State Seminoles men's basketball team''' represented [[Florida State University]] during the [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Seminoles were led by head coach [[Leonard Hamilton]], in his 19th year, and played their home games at the [[Donald L. Tucker Civic Center|Donald L. Tucker Center]] on the university's [[Tallahassee, Florida]] campus as members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]. The Seminoles entered the year as the defending conference champions and were picked to finish the season third in the league with [[Scottie Barnes]] and [[M. J. Walker]] receiving pre-season recognition.{{cite web|title=Virginia Named 2020-21 ACC Men's Basketball Preseason Favorite|url=https://theacc.com/news/2020/11/10/virginia-named-2020-21-acc-mens-basketball-preseason-favorite.aspx|publisher=Atlantic Coast Conference|date=November 11, 2020|accessdate=November 12, 2020}} The Seminoles finished the season 18–7, and 11–4 in [[2020–21 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]], to finish in second place. As the second seed in the [[2021 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] they earned a bye into the Quarterfinals where they advanced due to COVID-19 issues over [[2020–21 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]], defeated [[2020–21 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]] in the semifinals, but lost to [[2020–21 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball team|Georgia Tech]] in the Finals. They earned an at-large bid to the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as a four seed in the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament#East Regional|East Region]]. They defeated 13-seed [[2020–21 UNC Greensboro Spartans men's basketball team|UNC Greensboro]] in the first round and 5-seed [[2020–21 Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball team|Colorado]] in the second round before losing to 1-seed [[2020–21 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]] in the Sweet Sixteen. [[Scottie Barnes]], Balsa Koprivica, and [[RaiQuan Gray]] went on to be selected in the [[2021 NBA draft]].{{cite web|title=Barnes Picked No. 4 By Toronto Raptors In NBA Draft|url=https://seminoles.com/barnes-picked-no-4-by-orlando-magic-in-nba-draft/|publisher=Florida State University Athletics|date=July 29, 2021|accessdate=July 30, 2021}}{{cite web|title=Koprivica To Detroit; Gray to Nets in NBA Draft|url= https://seminoles.com/koprivica-to-detroit-gray-to-nets-in-nba-draft/|publisher=Florida State University Athletics|date=July 30, 2021|accessdate=July 31, 2021}} ==Previous season== The [[2019–20 Florida State Seminoles men's basketball team|Seminoles]] finished the [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20 season]] with a record of 26–5, 16–4 in ACC play, to finish in first place. The [[2020 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] was canceled prior to the team beginning play. The [[2020 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] was subsequently canceled as well due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic|coronavirus pandemic]].{{cite web|title=Florida State Athletics Announces Suspension Of Spring Sports|url=https://seminoles.com/florida-state-athletics-announces-suspension-of-spring-sports/|publisher=Florida State University|date=March 12, 2020|accessdate=March 12, 2020}} Florida State ended the season ranked in the top five of both polls. On March 14, 2020, the Florida State Senate declared the Florida State Seminoles as the national champions for the 2019–2020 season.{{cite web|title=Florida Senate legislation declares Florida State the 2020 men's basketball national champion|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/florida-senate-legislation-declares-florida-state-the-2020-mens-basketball-national-champion/|work=CBS Sports|date=March 14, 2020|accessdate=March 14, 2020}} [[Patrick Williams (basketball)|Patrick Williams]], [[Devin Vassell]], and [[Trent Forrest]] would go on to participate in the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite web|title=3 Seminoles feature in 2020 NBA draft|url=https://www.wtxl.com/sports/college-sports/fsu/3-seminoles-feature-in-2020-nba-draft|publisher=ABC WTXL, Channel 27|date=November 18, 2020|accessdate=November 19, 2020}} ==Offseason== ===Departures=== {| class="wikitable sortable" border="1" style="text-align:center;" !
